event.name: UFC 330
event.notes: Discovery pulls recent uploads from each capper channel and keeps the ones whose title matches settings.discovery.title_contains. Add entries to "videos" only to pin a specific video by hand.

comments.comment: Both are grappling-heavy but Orolbai has the better gas tank, striking and scrambling to wear Wells down, finishing him in round two or three.

Orolbai is better than Wells at everything Wells does best, should take him down instantly and maul him on top; capper thinks he should be a much larger favorite and calls him the overwhelmingly confident pick to open the card.
He hasn't bet yet but plans to wait for full markets and play the Orolbai side, citing Orolbai's traits and upside.
Sees it as a bit of a mismatch: Orolbai is sharper and more dangerous on the feet, and unless Wells gets an early finish Orolbai wins nine times out of ten.
Said Orolbai wins by any means necessary, any way he wants, with no hesitation ('there's the deep dive').
Orolbai should find the takedowns and keep Wells down; Wells is a striker with lacking takedown defense, making it a bad stylistic matchup.
Barboza is 40, slower and less durable after a bad knockout loss; Ribovics is clean, durable and busy, has never really lost to a striker and should stay a step ahead.
He already bet the Ribovics moneyline around -400; Ribovics is young, insanely tough and high volume while Barboza is old, washed and coming off eye surgery.
He's 'kind of just feeling Ribovics' because Barboza, while sharper and more versatile, isn't there physically or health-wise.
Stated as his main card pick to defeat Barboza.
Barboza is on a three-fight losing skid and Ribovics's forward pressure and gunslinging boxing will be too much.
Ribovics is younger, bigger and will pressure with volume; Barboza has been chinned in several recent fights and Ribovics has enough power to break him down.
Doesn't mind the chalk even on short notice; Alvarez can make it a war that Njokuani can't win and lacks the power to earn Alvarez's respect.
Alvarez's fatal flaw is takedown defense and Njokuani never wrestles, so Alvarez gets the long-range striking match he wants against a hesitant opponent.
Already bet Alvarez at 2-to-1; he has huge upside on the ground and with standing guillotines, is more durable, and Njokuani has always been vulnerable grappling.
Taking the short-notice fight signals Alvarez is healthy and was in camp, and he's the better, bigger striker with lightweight skill while Njokuani consistently underwhelms.
Slight lean to Alvarez because his ground game is better; striking is close but the grappling should be the deciding factor.

picks.selection: Mansur Abdul-Malik by KO/TKO in round 1 or 2

comments.comment: Stoltzfus falls into the category of fighters Abdul-Malik can bang with, find the big shot and knock out as he jumps back into the win column.
Abdul-Malik has too many physical advantages; unless Stoltzfus consistently controls the grappling, Abdul-Malik lands the cleaner, more damaging shots.
Abdul-Malik's power and brutal ground and pound against Stoltzfus' bad chin, poor striking defense and poor takedown defense should equal a knockout.
Abdul-Malik is better technically on the feet, far more powerful and explosive, and his takedown defense removes Stoltzfus's best weapon; very confident.
Stoltzfus is chinny and there to be chinned; Abdul-Malik has the athleticism/power edge and finishes cleanly once he hurts someone.
Believes he's too fast on the feet and should score a KO/TKO in the first or second round.
Ribovics is ten years younger and closer to his prime, landing the bigger shots and countering Barboza's Muay Thai for a knockout.
Barboza's striking will shine at times, but Ribovics' pace and constant forward pressure should swing momentum and create the bigger shots.
Barboza is a longtime favorite of Adam's but his chin is completely gone; Adam calls it an easy pick for a quick, brutal first-round knockout.
Barboza is too old and has taken too much damage, and Ribovics gets a pure striking matchup with no takedown threat, so he should knock him out early in round one or two.
Ribovics' pressure, volume and power should overwhelm a 40-year-old Barboza who has taken a lot of damage; no specific round given since it could come in any of the three.
Expects the win to come most likely by KO.
Barboza is old and declining while Ribovics is closer to his prime with pressure and volume; unsure about paying -540.
Ribovics closes distance and takes away Barboza's kicking game; Barboza gets rocked and damaged in every fight now, so expects a round one TKO.
Expects the volume and kicks to wear Barboza down for a TKO by the end of round two.
He expects Ribovics to walk Barboza down, cut off the cage and touch his chin for a relatively easy knockout.

Both cappers pick Mansur: Angelo cites a giant grappling gap plus powerful hands and desperation after his TKO loss, while Jacob thinks the striking edge is the difference since Stoltzfus is stationary and hittable.
He hasn't bet it yet but says he's probably going to at four-to-one odds, seeing it as a tough physical/athletic matchup for Stoltzfus.
Picks Abdul-Malik to defeat Stoltzfus.
Abdul-Malik is far better on the feet and Stoltzfus's striking is unimpressive; should be an easy win.
Says he isn't super confident but Abdul-Malik is younger, more physical, with height, reach and power advantages over a hittable Stoltzfus.
Even though he thinks Abdul-Malik is a bottom-feeder middleweight, he's a fast athlete with power and decent takedown defense against a slow, chinnable Stoltzfus.
Dern is better everywhere - striking, grappling, even wrestling - and is all-time tough; Robertson has no path without takedowns, and capper says he can't see how she wins.

He refuses to believe Robertson is the better grappler, gives Dern the edge on the feet as well, and is surprised the line is only -215 with money coming in on Robertson; he may wait for a better number.
Thinks Dern dominates the grappling exchanges and gets it done.
Nick calls it a nightmare matchup for Robertson, saying Dern is better everywhere, has the striking and durability edge and could even land takedowns of her own.
Likes the Dern line as just, considering her the faster, harder striker and the better grappler in a bad stylistic matchup for Robertson, but admits he hasn't placed the bet because he's scared.

Leg one of the Slam of the Week: he thinks Dern is simply the better fighter, will sweep Robertson off top position and dominate with world-class jiu-jitsu, plus she's hungry as new champion and won't want to lose the belt.
Dern has faced a far better level of competition, is physically much bigger and stronger, and Robertson's takedown/ground-and-pound game won't hold her down.
Picks Dern in the co-main event.
States he is very confident: Robertson won't out-grapple or submit Dern, her striking is non-existent, and Dern is the far more physical, aggressive striker who should win nine times out of ten.
Orolbai is durable and went straight for grappling attacks in his last fight; 40-year-old Wells has little path outside a fluke KO.
Says Orolbai will smoke and submit Wells, pointing to Wells getting put to sleep by Carlston Harris and being folded up in round one.
Wells won't handle Orolbai's grappling as the fight wears on; Orolbai has the edge in both striking volume/technique and wrestling, so he should reach a dominant position and find the sub.
Calls it the easiest pick on the card: Orolbai is far better on the ground, has wins over ranked opposition, and Wells will get taken down and submitted or rocked into a panic takedown into a d'arce.
Thinks Orolbai will hunt a finish this time after going to decision last time out, and gets it via chain wrestling into a submission.
Finds the under 1.5 at +135 the way to go instead of -650; Stoltzfus is the type Abdul-Malik beats and his athleticism/power should produce an early first-round knockout.
Sam thinks he cooks Stoltzfus inside a round and says the under also has value at plus money.

picks.fight: Ian Machado Garry vs Islam Makhachev

comments.comment: It may be more competitive than the odds indicate, but nothing stops Makhachev from getting to his Dagestani wrestling; he wears Garry down and wins on the scorecards.
Included as a leg in his round-robin bet; he frames Makhachev as winning and cementing his legacy.

Expects Makhachev's superior trip/body-lock takedown arsenal (like Shavkat's success late) to control Garry to a 49-46/48-47 decision, though Garry's takedown defense and range make it tougher than the JDM fight.

He's clearly backing Islam ('we can't lose... let's get the win'), saying the face-off made him more confident because Islam looked noticeably bigger and stronger while Garry looked flimsy, and that once Islam gets him to the ground it's going to be a problem; he laments the -400 price being long.
Garry will have success at range, but over five rounds Makhachev's adaptability and constant grappling threats should take over, and extended top time makes it hard for Garry to recover.
Leg two of the Slam of the Week: calls Makhachev the best fighter in the world, 29-1, still in his prime with undiminished athleticism and a better chin at 170, while Garry can't finish anything.
Picks Makhachev in the main event.
Makhachev's wrestling and pressure are too much; Garry won't stop the takedowns and Makhachev's striking is good enough to hold his own.

He says he's leaning with Makhachev and can't pick against him — underrated boxing, elite defensive striking, and by far the better wrestler/grappler, though he acknowledges a Garry head-kick KO is the main upset path.

picks.fight: Ian Machado Garry vs Islam Makhachev
picks.selection: Islam Makhachev by submission in round 3

comments.comment: Doesn't rate Garry's stand-up; expects Makhachev to get takedowns and cage control like the Shavkat fight and hunt a finish (darce choke) after his flat JDM performance.
He thinks Garry survives to the third but gets taken down and choked out, so submission in round 3.
Says the massive athleticism gap makes this free money even at -375, calls it a max bet and thinks Wint finishes in three minutes or less.
Calls it a lock — Radev should put volume on Barboza and piece him up, despite not being phenomenal himself.
Lists it as a decent price prop to target given he expects an early submission.
Since he's picking Brahimaj and Brahimaj is submission-or-bust, the finish should come early.

He believes Hassan is vastly technically superior and will smell blood and finish inside two and a half minutes; getting plus money (+130/+140) for it is great value, and he called it the best value in that matchup.

picks.selection: Tresean Gore by submission in round 1

comments.comment: Called it his pick of the week at even money: Luque is finishable and less durable/driven now, while Gore hits hard, has sick submissions and proved himself by finishing Azamat Bekoev.

picks.fight: Yadier del Valle vs Darren Elkin

comments.comment: His official pick that he has played: Elkins grinds out del Valle, survives the chokes and wins a decision.

One of the two straight moneylines he likes: Pegliaro's 6-inch height and 4-inch reach edge, improved back-foot fighting and grappling defense should let him maintain range, counter Mulumba and possibly finish him.
He agreed with a viewer that Luque is a live dog and confirmed he picked Luque straight up as an underdog on UFC 330.

picks.selection: Anthony Wint in round 1 by KO

comments.comment: Former NFL player and genetic specimen with big power in his hands; will play the round 1 KO as soon as props are posted.
Angelo says Oralby is a different level of wrestler and will dominate a 40-year-old Wells whenever he wants; the odds are understated but too expensive to bet heavily.
Calls Magny a 'mandatory selection' as a crafty underdog; Bahamondes is mid, hasn't beaten anyone good and got controlled by Punahele Soriano, while Magny has only lost to good competition.
Refuses to break it down; says Stoltzfus is simply a victim and Barnaoui will beat him.
He has played the decision prop, believing Sutherland makes it hard for Montana to get on top and finish him.
Wint is a former NFL athlete with all knockouts while Adams has been knocked out multiple times; Adam calls it an easy pick and expects a contract.
Shorter, more compact, better wrestling and far more cage experience; will do anything to win, and the line is crashing toward favorite.
He already bet Gamrot on instinct when it was the only line up and still thinks he wins, largely trusting Gamrot's durability and grinding.
He's already committed to her moneyline from closer to -250 and thinks she should win, likely by finish down the stretch.
He was committed to Aspelund's moneyline and thinks his volume eventually corrals Pat into the cage and overwhelms him; he's unimpressed with Pat's movement.
He bet the moneyline because Sutherland wins the physical and athletic battle against an inexperienced opponent who needs the fight on the ground.
He already played her at better prices and still likes the moneyline; he expects her to win by decision or submission but won't commit to a prop since Lemos can steal rounds.

picks.fight: Ian Machado Garry vs Islam Makhachev
picks.selection: Fight does not go the distance

comments.comment: Jacob wanted Islam inside the distance at +150 but took fight doesn't go the distance at +120 to also cover a weird Garry finish; he expects Islam to wear Garry down and submit him.
Calls the moneyline free as well, though he prefers the under.
Regional finishers tend to fizzle out in the UFC and McConico's BJJ black belt/durability should get him past the first; he won't bet Johnson at -220 so the over 1.5 is the spot.
Expects Malumba to swing wildly and land a giant overhand; thinks Pegalurulo looks like he'll get highlight-reel knocked out and looked nervous at the faceoff.
Attacking a wide line — not because McConico is great, but Johnson looks poor in extended fights at 185 with his small frame.
Jacob says McConico is the better, more technical fighter with better takedown and submission defense, while Dante's striking is sloppy and gas tank questionable; he bet him.
He threw money on McConico, citing question marks with Dante Johnson and McConico's kicking range, grinding ability and all-around skills.
McConico is more technical with height and reach, better from range, and should stop most of Johnson's takedowns while picking him apart.
Disliked Johnson's footwork and hand movement against Cody Brundage; thinks McConico is the craftier fighter who can pick his way back in rounds two and three if he survives early.

picks.selection: Joel Alvarez by submission in round 1

comments.comment: Says he'll likely put money down at -200; Njokuani is on a two-fight losing streak and has been finished quickly recently, so Alvarez takes his back or gets an arm triangle early.

picks.selection: Jose Ochoa by KO/TKO in round 2

comments.comment: Johnson gets wobbly when hit clean, was knocked out by Alex Perez and stopped by Asu Almabayev a month ago with little prep time, and Ochoa hits hard.
Named Magny as one of the underdogs he picked straight up on the UFC 330 card.
Named as one of the underdogs he picked straight up on the UFC 330 card.
Sam has taken the under expecting Dern to finish, likely by submission.
His most confident favorite on the card for a long time - he wins by almost any means he chooses - but the odds have become extremely expensive.
Listed as one of the two straight moneylines he likes on the card; he expects Escadega's grappling defense to hold up and for him to take over on the feet and eventually find a knockout.
Another 'crafty dog' — thinks Giles is still chinnable and will walk onto something dumb, and he won't write Luque off as cooked yet.
Power vs pressure matchup where he trusts Orazbai to stay disciplined, use clinch work and relentless takedowns to drain Wells and take over as the rounds go on.
Says the opponent has been out-grappled, subbed and is susceptible to pressure, and Alvarez training with Islam should look solid and get the sub.

picks.selection: Jose Ochoa by KO/TKO in round 2

comments.comment: Ochoa's aggression and durability should overwhelm the hittable Johnson, who leaves too many openings, leading to a knockout.
He expects Ochoa to just throw hands and knock Johnson out early, in the first or second round, rather than go for a submission.
Ochoa's rare power at 125 will get Johnson's respect, Johnson is coming off a bad KO loss and fighting too often, and he won't offensively wrestle Ochoa.
Expects the win most likely by KO.
Vowed never to pick Johnson again; Johnson is hittable to the left hook and starts slow, while Ochoa has crisp boxing and in his view beat Alibayev.
Leans Ochoa: aggressive southpaw with power who will put the declining, recently-finished Johnson on the back foot and land the left hand on his open right side.
Interested in Johnson's finishing potential; his speed and early aggression should find the opening even if McConico has moments in the clinch.
Considered the McConico underdog but capped his card at three dogs; picks Johnson to KO him because McConico doesn't take damage well and only went to a near-split with Johnson previously.
Adam takes Johnson by knockout but says he isn't convinced and wouldn't be shocked if Johnson dropped an ugly decision after his close fight with Brundage.
Johnson's boxing is his real skill set and McConico hates being backed up and hit; the worry is Johnson's terrible fight IQ leading him to wrestle again.
Johnson's explosiveness, power and speed should matter in the striking exchanges and get an early finish, but McConico is the more technical guy and very live as a dog; low to mid confidence.
Adam thinks Abdul-Malik is somewhat overrated but Stolz is super chinny, so he fades Stolz and takes Abdul-Malik by knockout.

picks.selection: Bal Hassan by KO/TKO in round 1

comments.comment: Adam sees no point to the matchmaking and expects Hassan to knock out the Road to UFC knockout victim in the first round and get a contract.
Adam thinks Kudman should win this fight, probably by submission.

He predicts a submission (initially round one) but says he'd play submission flat rather than a round because he doesn't fully trust her wrestling; he thinks she gets it to the mat and is better there.
He thinks her skills lead to a submission finish, noting she nearly finished Carli Judice in rounds one and three.

picks.selection: Gamrot point spread (to survive/win on points)

comments.comment: The spread prices are extremely tight and he thinks even if Gamrot loses he survives, so the spread plugs into his over play.

picks.fight: Billy Ray Goff vs Tai Miller

comments.comment: He bet Miller when it was the only market available; he thinks Miller wins the jousting battle, moves better and takes the outside striking exchanges.
Undefeated 10-0 A-side with strong training partners at Elevation and Jackson Wink, though unproven.
He expects a finish eventually but not early, since Wells has real submission defense and Bai's quick finishes came against guys without it.
Already bet the over to cover his Ochoa-by-decision prediction, trusting Charles Johnson's traits to survive and rally in round three.
He has a lot of faith in Gamrot's durability and thinks the fight is more likely to go long/go the distance.

picks.fight: Yadier del Valle vs Darren Elkin

comments.comment: Sentimentality and bias, plus he thinks Elkins is very hard to choke and can grind, pop his head out of chokes and scramble better.

picks.fight: Billy Ray Goff vs Tai Miller

comments.comment: He played the over, thinking the fight goes long and that any finish would come in the second half.
He bet Nurgai because he's his pick and the odds were tight enough; if Nurgai wins he expects a knockout.
He bet the over, liking Miranda's durability and both fighters' skill sets; he likes Sosa to win but doesn't love it.

picks.selection: John Cunnaman by submission (club and sub)

comments.comment: Predicts a club-and-sub finish against Cropshot's wrestling gaps, though he'd stay away from the under here.

picks.selection: Esteban Ribovics by KO in round 1

comments.comment: 40-year-old Barboza is on a three-fight losing streak and will shell up as Ribovics lands more and more before finishing him early.

picks.selection: Mounir Lazzez by submission in round 1

comments.comment: Lazzez should sting the nearly 40-year-old Wells on the feet, force a panic takedown, reverse it and take his back for a first-round rear naked choke.
Crafty underdog pick — Turner doesn't take damage well, will get leg-kicked and his offense will fade after round one, and he doesn't respect Turner's recent Barboza win.
Nick doesn't trust Turner's fight IQ and notes Fernandes is well-rounded, hard to finish and has never been stopped, so he can weather the early storm.
Fernandes mixes pressure, combinations and takedowns well and can close distance to take away Turner's range; he picked him but didn't place the bet.
Already bet Fernandes; he's surging, more technically sound striking and sharper kicks, while Turner has durability issues and doubts after retiring off a loss.
Fernandes is a good game planner on a three-fight streak who stayed active, while Turner retired, has lost 3 of 5 and only beat an end-of-career Barboza; great price at +148.
Doesn't fully trust Turner's comeback after his early retirement, and Fernandes is solid, well-rounded and mixes in takedowns well; likely decision or late TKO, but a lower confidence pick.
If Malumba is winning it's early, so he's inclined to believe the under.
Urbay is the better wrestler (19 takedowns vs Chris Curtis) and Wells isn't enough of a submission threat; Urbay has been finding second-round submissions.
The line has moved from -600 to a pick'em, and Adam likes the former underdog to win, probably by decision.
Adam takes the dog, saying Balumba is too wild and Pagliarulo, who comes from PFL and Cage Titans, can knock him out.
He entertains picking Gaethje but lands on Islam because Islam is strong and talented.
Gorimbo has a head like a brick, while Luque tends to chop away with good footwork.
Adam MMA told him it's a free slate at -2000 so he threw him into a $50 parlay, though he warns against the -525 under.

He predicts Orolbai wins by decision since Wells has never been knocked out and is skilled enough to survive, so the over fits, though he admits Orolbai is dangerous enough that he can't fully trust it.
He lands on Kanuto because of her distinct grappling/submission edge and says he likes her at two-to-one odds, though he won't bet heavily and would play her if she's the underdog.

picks.selection: Gillian Robertson by submission in round 2

comments.comment: Going with his gut on an upset: Dern feels like she could lose any fight, and Robertson is on a long win streak with great reversals and submissions from the bottom; armbar finish.
Fernando is big, fast, 6'3 with 81.5in reach, believing in his hands after recent KOs, while Tobias looked lost when he couldn't get the fight down.
Admits he hasn't watched Fernando fight, but thought Tobias looked mid in his last outing, so takes Fernando by KO.
Tobias looked awful and not UFC-ready in his debut, so Adam takes Fernando to win by TKO.
Fernando's striking is cleaner and more powerful with a huge reach advantage, while Tobias relies on takedowns that failed against Da'Mon Blackshear; he sees a second or third round finish.
Thinks the fight should be even odds and Tobias is value, but ultimately Fernando is the more complete, technical and versatile striker; explicitly a low confidence pick.
Fernando is a massive LFA double champion with power and better level of competition, and Tobias struggles on the feet and plods around, so he expects a first-round knockout.
Expects the size, power and finishing potential to show up early for a first-round TKO.

picks.selection: Bilal Hassan in round 1 by KO

comments.comment: Says Hassan wins by round 1 KO given the weak opposition, but explicitly says not to take the expensive under.
High confidence in Ochoa but the price has run away from him, so he only greenlights him as part of a chalk parlay.
Thinks he runs away with the fight against Wells and likely finds a submission, but the price has zoomed too high for a standalone play so it's only a chalk parlay leg.
Expects a round-one KO from his huge athleticism as he bounces back from his first MMA loss, but the price is too short so only a chalk parlay leg.
Angelo says Luque is better everywhere and the line movement making him a dog makes no sense, but he is only picking him, not betting him.
Johns is his pick and he says the moneyline (or Johns over a round and a half) would be the smart play, though he hasn't pulled the trigger on the juicy round props.

picks.selection: Themba Gorimbo by KO in round 1

comments.comment: He thinks Gorimbo has too much power for Luque's questionable chin and touches it early, calling a first-round KO.
Luque is the better fighter everywhere and too good a submission artist, though the capper isn't confident and may flip later in the week.
Total is a pick'em and he leans slightly toward the over in this one.

picks.selection: Juliana Miller to win in round 2 or 3

comments.comment: He likes her round two and three prowess and would play the flat round two/three finish at +300 since she's more likely to win late.

picks.selection: Steven Aspelund to finish in round 2 or 3

comments.comment: He threw sprinkles on the flat round two and three finish lines, expecting a late TKO rather than an early one.

picks.selection: Carol Furro to win in round 2 or 3

comments.comment: He'll throw sprinkles on a late Furro finish if the odds are juicy, since Furro's body work and proven 15-minute cardio could break Kanuto down late.

picks.fight: Yadier del Valle vs Darren Elkin
picks.selection: Darren Elkins to win in round 2 or 3

comments.comment: Hail Mary sprinkles on rounds two and three, with round three finish available at big odds.

picks.selection: Ramiz Brahimaj by submission in round 1

comments.comment: 12 of Brahimaj's 13 wins are submissions, mostly in round one, and if he beats Magny it is far and away by submission, so he plans to play that prop.
Magny has been submitted repeatedly, often in round one, and Brahimaj has ten first-round submission wins and constantly attacks chokes.
The fight only goes two ways: Brahimaj by submission or Magny by decision, so take the juiced submission payout instead of the moneyline.
Brahimaj only wins by submission and usually in round one, and Magny has always struggled with submission defense; the fight is either a Brahimaj finish or a Magny decision.
Even-odds fight but he favors Brahimaj's explosiveness and quick finishing ability, and Magny has repeatedly gotten into bad grappling spots and been submitted recently.
Magny is 39 and has been caught in chokes in his recent fights, while Brahimaj is a strong submission artist who should find Magny's neck.
Thinks Brahimaj keeps Magny on the ground and sinks in some type of submission.

picks.selection: Jalin Turner by KO/TKO in round 1

comments.comment: Leaning on Turner's speed, length and power to counter the calf kicks, stop the takedowns and eventually find a knockout.
Turner should have the cleaner early moments, punish Fernandez's entries with straight shots and knees, and eventually his size and power make the difference.
Turner is the side whenever he faces a non-wrestler, he's enormous for 155, his fights rarely leave round one, and the odds are close.
Leaning on Turner's explosiveness, size and much better level of competition, but calls him untrustworthy mentally and wouldn't jump on the line yet.
Calls it a 60/40 fight; Turner's aggression, size and clinch elbows/knees should get a finish in the first three minutes, otherwise Fernandes wins.
Surprised Magny is the dog since Brahimaj isn't the grappling level of Amosov or Burns; Magny should defend early submissions and take over as Brahimaj's gas tank fades.
Jacob takes the dog Magny as the safer pick, saying it's a tailor-made Magny fight where he weathers the early submission threat and wears Brahimaj down for the decision.
Thinks Brahimaj is overrated with wins only over cans, while Magny has huge height/reach, experience and a grappling edge and can pick him apart off the back foot for a decision.
Doesn't think Brahimaj has any top-level wins or the power to finish Magny, and expects Magny to clinch him up against the cage and control him on top; odds are close.
Luque is the more experienced, technically better fighter and Gore has durability questions, so he takes the underdog shot on the veteran at a good number.

Luque is on the downswing but not washed and is the better fighter everywhere; he'll piece Gore up on the feet and is too slick a grappler to be taken down cleanly. Capper is waiting for the line to stall out before actually betting.
Already bet Luque, believing he is the better man on the feet and in scrambles and will chew Gore up inside hook range, where Gore has been hurt before.
He suggests the round 1 prop because it could come as a knockout, a club-and-sub, or a submission off a back take — he expects Turner to get it done early.
Turner has zero decision wins in 15 victories and most of his finishes come in round one; Sam expects him to knock out or submit Fernandes early, saying 'don't get cute with it' at +250.
He expects Turner to come out like a madman, pin Fernandes on the cage and finish him early; if it gets past round one Fernandes becomes live.
Expects Brahimaj to rush the guillotine/front choke early against a fighter who gets into precarious positions in the first round.
Jacob says he will definitely have action on Brahimaj early — first or second round submission — since Brahimaj chases the guillotine relentlessly and Magny is lazy with his head position.
Expects Fernando to outlast and chop down the 23-year-old Tobias with diverse striking, so he'll reach for the round two and three finish props rather than the short moneyline price.
Fernando has a 7-inch reach and height edge, wins on the feet, and Tobias has been knocked out before and didn't look great in his debut.
He feels Fernando can find a finish, calling it a second-round finish.
Coming off a loss, Sam expects Abdul-Malik to blow the doors off Stoltzfus early and reassert his athleticism, so round-one KO is the play.
He expects Abdul-Malik to dominate and find an early finish, probably first round.
Both like Fernando's striking, length and athleticism over Tobias's brute-force grappling, but at -300 in a UFC debut they are picking him without betting the moneyline.
Fernando has slick Muay Thai with heavy calf kicks and should stop Tobias's pressure and takedowns to pick him apart standing.
Fernando is the bigger, more athletic man with an 80-inch reach, better finishing ability, good low kicks and momentum from two first-round finishes in LFA.
Robertson's submission-over-position mentality gets her in trouble and Dern will punish it; Dern creates scrambles and submits off her back, so he predicts Dern retains by submission.
Even off her back Dern threatens Robertson, and Sam calls +205 a decent number for the submission.
Dern has the striking edge and Robertson's grappling will put her in submission danger; leaning Dern but waiting on weigh-ins and face-offs.
Robertson lacks the power to hurt Dern on the feet and will shoot takedowns into Dern's elite jiu-jitsu; expects an armbar.
Alvarez took the fight on short notice but can dominate; while he could land the big shot, his submission game is what finishes Njokuani.
If Alvarez can get past Njokuani's striking and force grappling exchanges, his submission game from unusual positions eventually takes over.
Alvarez is better everywhere and has only lost to elite fighters while Njokuani just lost to Carlos Leal; one takedown and the fight is over, and the submission price offers plus money.
Njokuani is a striker who struggles badly once the fight hits the mat and has a poor get-up game, while Alvarez is a prolific early submission finisher.
Floats that Alvarez may even get the finish by submission.
Njokuani has been submitted recently (Jake Matthews) and Alvarez should blitz then find takedowns into a submission.

picks.fight: Ian Machado Garry vs Islam Makhachev
picks.selection: Islam Makhachev by submission in round 4

comments.comment: He expects Makhachev to get takedowns and choke Garry out, and is putting money on the submission at +200.
He repeatedly says he thinks the arm triangle happens: once Islam opens the Garry lock and passes to half guard and mount, Garry hasn't shown the ability to scramble up off his back.
Nobody defends Makhachev's takedowns and Garry lacks one-punch power, so Garry would have to win a decision; Makhachev drags him late for a finish.
Despite giving Garry a 35-40% chance and outlining a game plan for him, he still picks Islam by submission, believing Islam should be able to secure takedowns and control time.

Makhachev has solved every advantage Garry has before (size, reach, boxing), is elite in scrambles with the d'arce and back takes, and Garry can't finish him or out-decision him with Khabib game-planning.
Jacob finds +300 interesting because Wells puts himself in bad grappling positions and Oralby can snatch a submission when Wells tries to scramble.
Oralbay is too dominant and once he gets it to the mat it's a finish; Wells' grappling camp could drag it to a decision, so he may switch to the decision after weigh-ins.
Johnson tends to give away the first round which is fatal in a 15-minute fight, and Ochoa's pressure, volume, power and speed should carry it; capper doesn't love the -335 price.
Johnson is washed with a shaky chin while Ochoa is younger, quicker, hungrier and more powerful.
Picks Ochoa to beat Johnson in the featured fight.

picks.selection: Myktybek Orolbai by KO/TKO in round 2 or round 3

comments.comment: Orolbai does what Wells does but better with a far superior gas tank, so once his pressure wears Wells down he should find the finish after round one; the moneyline is -900 so mixing round 2/3 KO props is how to squeeze profit.
The under at even money is calling his name because Ribovics will put immediate pace and pressure on the 40-year-old Barboza and find his chin early; better than taking the big chalk.

picks.selection: Fight does not go to decision

comments.comment: Plans to double dip; Gore has been hurt repeatedly and Luque can counter and finish, making a non-decision likely.
Both men are tough and have been in extended fights and decisions; neither is a kill-or-be-killed heavyweight type, so the fight should last past round one.

picks.selection: Dante Johnson in round 1 by KO

comments.comment: Happy to play both sides: Johnson's fastest, most dangerous path is an early KO, so +350 for round one is worth it.
Luque's prime is behind him and his chin is questionable; Gorimbo has slick hands, power, and enough grappling to stop takedowns and keep it standing.
Luque is the technically superior fighter and, as long as his durability holds, should counter Gore and find a clinch/submission opportunity.
Luque has fought far better competition and just beat Kelvin Gastelum; his jiu-jitsu is levels above Gore's, so once he gets a takedown it's a wrap.

A 50/50 fight where he takes the underdog: Luque is arguably better everywhere technically and if he hurts his opponent he'll likely club-and-sub with a front choke, though he's worried about Luque's durability.
